title: Asking and Being Answered: Which Question Is This the Answer To

questions.question: A requester sends a command and takes the next response that arrives as the answer. The link sometimes delivers a response late. What happens?
options: Nothing, a late response is dropped
A late response can be taken as the answer to a later request, and the real answer then shifts onto the one after, until a timeout resynchronises them
questions.explanation: Measured, 49 of 200 answers were wrong. Every message was valid, so no error is raised anywhere.

questions.question: With ids, no answer was wrong, yet the device ended at 227 instead of 200. Why?
options: A resend is a repeated command: the answer was what was lost, the device had already done it, and it did it again, 27 times
The late responses added to the position
questions.explanation: The overshoot equals the number of resends exactly. Matching ids is the requester's half; the device has a half too.

questions.question: What does the ReplyCache do when a request arrives with the id of the last one answered?
options: Executes it again to be safe
Replays the answer it gave before and does not repeat the act
questions.explanation: The requester cannot tell whether the request or its answer was lost. The device can tell it has seen this id, and replaying is what makes a resend harmless.

questions.question: Why does a retry keep the same id?
options: The id is how the device recognises a repeat, so a fresh one makes a resend look like a different command and the cache stops working
questions.explanation: A retry is the same request sent again. A new id says it is a different one.

questions.question: Why is a failed send not allowed to start the request or use up an id?
options: It would make the ids irregular
The request never went out, so waiting out its timeouts is waiting for an answer to nothing, and the next id would skip a number for no reason
The id belongs to the port
questions.explanation: State should describe what happened on the wire. A request that was never sent is not Waiting.

questions.question: A command is "move to 200" instead of "move by one". Does the device need a ReplyCache?
options: Not for correctness: repeating an absolute move leaves the device in the same place, so the retry is harmless
questions.explanation: A command that is safe to repeat is idempotent. Designing commands that way is cheaper than remembering answers, and is the better fix where the protocol allows it.
